extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, their counsel, and USPTO OED personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order resolving disciplinary action against a registered patent attorney for false statements in admissions materials, describing the legal conclusions, mitigating/aggravating considerations, and the agreed sanctions and conditions for reinstatement under USPTO rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO jurisdiction for disciplinary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.20 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes statutory and regulatory basis for OED to initiate, approve settlements, and impose discipline on registered practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on dishonesty, fraud, deceit or misrepresentation (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit or misrepresentation — e.g., providing multiple false statements of material fact in applications for admission to the North Carolina State Bar and the USPTO registration examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: False statements of material fact in applications and related filings constitute actionable misconduct under § 11.804(c). The Order cites multiple false statements in the respondent's admission materials as triggering this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public discipline by a state authority as a basis for USPTO discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Be publicly disciplined on ethical or professional misconduct grounds by any duly constituted authority of a State — e.g., being disbarred by the North Carolina State Bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State-bar disciplinary findings (disbarment, suspension, etc.) can form the predicate for USPTO discipline; such state action is explicitly cited as a violation under § 11.804(h)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthfulness requirements in USPTO registration application and oath
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must certify truthfully (e.g., 'I certify that each and every statement or representation in this application is true and correct') and swear/affirm not to 'seek to mislead the officials of the Office by any artifice or false statements of fact or law.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Misrepresenting credentials (for example, fabricating a B.S. degree) on the application to sit for the USPTO registration examination or on subsequent Data Sheets and Oaths constitutes violation and grounds for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-reporting, acknowledgment, and cooperation as mitigating considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent self-reported to OED, acknowledged ethical lapses, demonstrated genuine contrition, accepted responsibility, and cooperated (including providing sua sponte supplemental responses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order treats self-reporting, acknowledgement of wrongdoing, contrition, and active cooperation with the investigation as mitigating factors when determining and negotiating sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior disciplinary history (or lack thereof) as a factor in sanctioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent had over twenty-four years of patent practice and 'has not been the subject of any disciplinary action before the USPTO.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An absence of prior USPTO disciplinary actions is identified as a mitigating factor in assessing appropriate sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension from practice before the USPTO (agreed term)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from practice before the Office for forty-eight (48) months commencing on the date the Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The suspension is immediate upon the Final Order and is an express agreed sanction for the misconduct found; it is a primary punitive/remedial measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension remains in effect until reinstatement petition granted (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall remain suspended from the practice of patent, trademark, and non-patent law before the USPTO until the OED Director grants a petition requesting Respondent's reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The suspension is both time-based (48 months) and contingent upon successful completion of the reinstatement process under the cited regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to conclude pending matters (37 C.F.R. § 11.58(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall be granted limited recognition pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(f) for thirty (30) days starting on the date of the Final Order so Respondent may endeavor to conclude work on behalf of clients on any matters pending before the Office; if work cannot be concluded within thirty (30) days, Respondent shall so advise each such client so that the client may make other arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short-term limited recognition may be granted to allow orderly transfer/closing of client matters, but requires notice to clients if not completed within the limited period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires adherence to the regulatory provisions governing resignation, suspension, and limited recognition procedures and duties to clients when practice status changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO customer numbers and electronic accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's name shall be dissociated from any Customer Number(s) and USPTO verified Electronic System account(s), and Respondent shall not apply for, obtain, nor have his name added [to] a USPTO Customer Number or a USPTO verified Electronic system account unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents suspended practitioner from accessing or appearing in USPTO electronic systems until reinstated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice and publication of disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at the OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided 'Notice of Suspension' text describing the grounds and sanction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public dissemination of the Final Order and a Gazette notice communicates the discipline to the public and profession and fulfills regulatory/publicity requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record may be used in future proceedings and as aggravating factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this Agreement or the Final Order shall prevent the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order: (1) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct concerning Respondent ... and (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding against Respondent (i) as an aggravating factor ... and/or (ii) to rebut any statement or representation by or on Respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prior settled disciplinary record can be cited in later complaints or proceedings to increase sanctions or counter claims of mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition for reinstatement in patent matters: demonstration of scientific/technical training
rubrics_metrics.description: As a condition of being reinstated to practice before the USPTO in patent matters, Respondent shall demonstrate that she possesses the scientific and technical training necessary to provide valuable service to patent applicants with any petition for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement petitions for patent practice must address both ethical rehabilitation and the technical qualifications necessary to competently practice in patent matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of appellate and reconsideration rights and allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent waives all rights to seek reconsideration of the Final Order under 37 C.F.R. § 11.56, waives the right to have the Final Order reviewed under 37 C.F.R. § 11.57, and waives the right otherwise to appeal or challenge the Final Order in any manner; each party shall bear their own costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A settlement can include waivers of procedural rights and agreement that each side bears its own costs, finalizing the resolution and precluding appeal-based relitigation.
